tools.description:
Full-text search over the official AGILEX product documentation.

        Use this first for any question about AGILEX hardware: pinouts, CAN
        protocol details, baud rate, firmware upgrade, error codes, LED/beep
        meanings, installation, calibration, SDK usage.

        Args:
            query: Chinese or English keywords. Include the product name
                (piper / pika / nero / ranger / limo / scout / bunker / hunter /
                tracer / umr) plus the concept, e.g. "piper CAN 波特率".
            limit: 1-25 results, default 8.
            space: optional space slug or name fragment to narrow the search,
                e.g. "agx-chassis-manual-cn-en" or "底盘使用手册".

        Returns JSON: {query, count, results:[{doc_id,title,space,url,score,chars,snippet}]}.
        ``count`` is the number of results in this reply (0-``limit``). A result
        whose title carries 【未发】/【暂不对外】 includes ``status_note``.
        ``doc_id`` is what ``get_doc`` expects.
tools.name: search_docs

tools.description:
Locate a passage *inside* one manual, without paging through it.

        Use this after ``search_docs`` whenever you need a specific table, command
        or error code rather than the whole page — including short documents,
        because manuals commonly open with a preamble and page 1 rarely answers a
        question. It returns the exact ``offset`` of each match, so one
        ``get_doc(doc_id, offset=...)`` lands on the right section.

        Prefer this over repeatedly calling ``get_doc`` with increasing offsets.

        Args:
            doc_id: id from ``search_docs`` (also accepts the page slug).
            query: the *concept*, not the product name — e.g. "波特率" or
                "急停 接线". Terms that already appear in this page's title are
                ignored, because ``search_docs`` picked the page by them; passing
                the product name again only adds noise. Generic words that appear
                in nearly every manual are down-weighted, so one distinctive term
                is enough.
            limit: 1-10 passages, default 5.

        Matching is OR, not AND: a passage is returned when it contains at least
        one term with enough weight. Terms that are absent from this page therefore
        do **not** force a zero result — check ``missing_terms`` to see which of
        your words this page never mentions, and ``matched_terms`` for the ones it
        does. A query made only of stop words (or nothing) returns ``count: 0``
        with a hint.

        Returns JSON: {doc_id,title,space,url,chars,query,count,returned,
        matched_terms,missing_terms,hits:[{offset,heading,score,matched,excerpt}],
        hint}. ``count`` is the total number of matched passages; ``returned`` is
        how many are in ``hits`` (capped by ``limit``). ``heading`` is the nearest
        heading above the passage; ``offset`` is absolute in the page body.
tools.name: find_in_doc

tools.description:
Read one documentation page as Markdown.

        Call this with a ``doc_id`` returned by ``search_docs`` (or a slug such as
        ``ymZimX7JLe``). Manuals are often 20k-60k characters, so this tool
        paginates: if the reply has ``truncated: true`` and a ``next_offset``,
        call again with that ``offset`` to continue. Do not re-request the same
        offset.

        Args:
            doc_id: id from search_docs (also accepts the page slug).
            max_chars: characters per call, default 20000, max 120000.
            offset: start position, default 0.

        Returns JSON: {doc_id,title,space,url,chars,offset,returned,max_chars,
        truncated,next_offset,updated_at,content}. Always cite ``url``.
        If the page has no body (folder or unwritten page), the reply has
        ``empty: true`` and a hint — do not retry with other offsets.
tools.name: get_doc

tools.description:
List documented pages, optionally inside one space.

        Use when the caller wants an inventory ("what manuals exist for ranger")
        rather than an answer.

        Args:
            space: optional space slug or name fragment.
            limit: 1-300, default 100.
            offset: pagination offset, must be >= 0.

        Returns JSON: {space, count, offset, docs:[{doc_id,title,space,url,chars}]}.
        ``count`` is the number of docs in this page; compare it with ``limit`` to
        decide whether to request the next page. There is no total field — use
        ``list_spaces`` for per-space counts.
tools.name: list_docs

tools.description:
List the public documentation spaces with page counts.

        Call this when the caller is unsure which product family a document
        belongs to, or to explain coverage.

        Returns JSON: {count, spaces:[{space,name,docs,chars}]}.
tools.name: list_spaces
